DESCRIPTION: A beach extending south from Quoraburagun Point for 2.5 km to Terrace Point within Ben Boyd National Park.
ORIGIN: Named after The Pinnacles, an erosion formation in this area.
HISTORY: Beach well-known locally by this name.  The beach was shown as `Long Beach` on the first edition of the Eden 1;25,000 topographical map.  However, the name was never assigned.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach about 1km N of Fly Roads and 0.3 km SE of Stephens Peak.
ORIGIN: This feature is known as `Wreck Beach` because of numerous wrecks on the beach.  (Crombie I National Parks and Wildlife Service officer proposal dated 3 July 1997)
HISTORY: This beach has been called `Wreck Beach` for minimum of twenty years. This name probably goes back to the time of settlement.  (Crombie I National Parks and Wildlife officer proposal dated 3 July 1997)

DESCRIPTION: A beach at Vincentia, located 1 km west of Plantation Point, and lying to the west of Barfleur Beach.
HISTORY: The name 'Orion Beach' once applied to the beach now known as 'Barfleur Beach'.  Later the name 'Orion Beach' was moved to a beach west of the present 'Barfleur Beach'.

DESCRIPTION: A beach at Norah Head, about 200 metres NW of Norah Head Lighthouse.
ORIGIN: This name commemorates the seven mariners who lost their lives on 5 December 1940, when the ship struck a mine off Norah Head.  The boat was the first Australian merchant ship to be sunk by German action on Australia's east coast.  (`Sun Weekly`  11 December 1997)
HISTORY: In December 1997, Cr Greg Best of Wyong Council proposed that the beach be renamed to honour the men who lost their lives.  (`Sun Weekly` 11 December 1997)

DESCRIPTION: A beach about 2 km south of Terrigal and about 4 km north by west of Tudibaring Head.  It is in Bulbararing Bay and adjacent to the suburb of North Avoca.  It is about 1 km long.
ORIGIN: Gosford Council proposed the name North Avoca Beach to the northern end of Avoca Beach, north of Avoca Lake.

DESCRIPTION: A beach on the western shore of Soldiers Point in Port Stephens.  It extends from Pearson Park in the south, approximately 567metres in a northerly direction to  a point adjacent to Resthaven Avenue.
ORIGIN: Named by the Soldiers Point/Salamander Bay Parks, Reserves and Halls Committee of Council.  The beach and adjacent park is a popular area for families to picnic and witness the spectacular sunset.
HISTORY: The small quiet beach was once primarily used for oyster farming.  The leases were bought out by the Cromarty Village Development who planned open public access onto the beach through Pearson Park.

DESCRIPTION: A beach adjacent to the Byron Bay Surf Club, it extends east to Clarkes Beach and west to Belongil Beach.
A beach N of Waniora Point and S of Bulli Point.
A beach S of Waniora Point and N of Billambi Beach.
A beach adjacent to the township of Tathra about 1 km W of Tathra Point.
A coastal beach extending northwards from Corindi Beach to Red Rock.
A beach approx 700m long situated midway between Short Point and Merimbula Point at the northern end of Merimbula Bay.
A beach approx 5 km long running in a NNE direction from Murunna Point  near the settlements of Wallaga Lake Heights and Akolele.
A beach at the eastern end of Horseshoe Bay. It is located about 600m NNW of Bermagui Trig Station.
A coastal beach approx. 1.8 km long extending north of Flat Top Point to Woolgoolga Headland.  Adjoins the suburb of Woolgoolga.
ORIGIN: Woolgoolga Back Beach takes it name from the township of Woolgoolga.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 3.5 km long extending north of Corindi River to Station Creek.  Adjoins Yuraygir National Park, locality of Barcoongere.
ORIGIN: Station Creek Beach takes it name from the historical locality of Station Creek.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 6.6 km extending north from the north entrance wall at Wooli Wooli River in the locality of Wooli  to Wilsons Head.
ORIGIN: Named after the locality of Wooli.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 3 km long extending north from Diggers Camp Beach to a rocky outcrop south of Tree Point at the village of Minnie Water.
ORIGIN: Named after the village of Minnie Water.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 1 km long adjacent to the village of Minnie Water and extending north to Rocky Point.
ORIGIN: Named after the village of Minnie Water.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 9 km long extending north from a rocky point at the Illaroo camping area to the southernmost rocks at Clay Head, Sandon.
ORIGIN: Named after the locality of Sandon at the mouth of the Sandon River.

DESCRIPTION: A beach about 0.75 km long on the coast of NSW about 1.25 km generally south south east of the Town of Ulladulla and 1.25 km west of Warden Head.
A beach about 1.3 km long located about 1 km ENE of Burrill Lake and about 1 km NE of Burrill Beach.
A beach about 800 metres long between Pinnacle Point and Hawks Nest Headland in the suburb of Surfside.
ORIGIN: Surfside Beach is named after the adjacent suburb of Surfside.

DESCRIPTION: A beach adjacent to the suburb of Windang between Perkins Beach to the north and Windang Island to the south.
ORIGIN: Windang Beach is adjacent to the suburb of Windang.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 3.5 kms long extending from the south wall of Cudgen Creek south to the southern extent of the suburb of Kingscliff.
ORIGIN: The coastline of the suburb of Kingscliff is divided into two parts north and south of the mouth of Cudgen Creek.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 200 metres long extending from the rocks and bluff that separate it from the southern end of Cabarita Beach south to Norries Head in the suburb of Cabarita Beach.
ORIGIN: Named after Norries Head.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 2.5 km long extending south from Norries Head to the mouth of Cudgera Creek.
ORIGIN: Named after Margaret Philomena Murnane (1863 - 1956) who was the first person to select land at Hastings Point in 1907. Maggie was an experienced mid-wife and assisted in many births in the district.  Later she conducted a small guest house. She became an expert fisherwoman.  Source:  Daily News 2 Nov 1999)

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 2km long, extending south from Cudgera Beach at the southern suburb boundary of Hastings Point to Black Rocks near the southern suburb boundary of Pottsville.
ORIGIN: Named after the suburb of Pottsville.

DESCRIPTION: A coastal beach approx. 4.5 km long situated between Mooball Beach to the north and Crabbes Creek Beach to the south.  The southern extent is the Tweed Shire LGA boundary.
MEANING: Grass.  (Richmond Tweed Regional Library 1984)  From: Gidabal and Yugambir dialects of Bundjalung.  (M Sharpe)
ORIGIN: Named after the adjacent beachfront locality of Wooyung.

DESCRIPTION: A beach approx. 200 metres long between Greenplay Point and Yachett Point in the suburb of Soldiers Point.
ORIGIN: Named after Mary Cromarty.  The Cromarty family were the first Europeans to settle on Soldiers Point circa 1828.  Capt. William Cromarty arrived in Australia in 1824 with his wife and two children born in Scotland.  Mary was their first Australian born child 1825. Capt. Cromarty traded between Port Stephens and Sydney, then in
HISTORY: 1833 was appointed as the Newcastle Pilot.  Following his death in a failed rescue mission off Fingal, Mary and her mother ran a business supplying provisions to locals and the crews of fishing vessels.

DESCRIPTION: A beach bordered in the south by Woolgoolga Beach, extending north to a point adjacent to the suburb of Safety Beach.
ORIGIN: The beach is adjacent to the suburb of Safety Beach.

DESCRIPTION: A beach bordered in the south by the north wall of Coffs Harbour and in the north by Coffs Creek.
ORIGIN: Named after its proximity to Coffs Harbour

DESCRIPTION: A beach bordered in the south by a rock outcrop adjacent to Wonga Park at 3rd Avenue Sawtell to Boambee Head in the north.
ORIGIN: Commemorates the late Cecil McLeod Murray, who established the first mechanical workshop in Sawtell.

DESCRIPTION: A beach bordered in the south by Bonville Headland, extending north to a rock outcrop adjacent to Wonga Park in the suburb of Sawtell.
ORIGIN: Named after its proximity to the suburb of Sawtell.

DESCRIPTION: A small beach located at Treharne Cove, 400 metres west of Longnose Point, Pittwater in the suburb of Ku-ring-gai Chase.
A beach located to the north of Barrenjoey Beach and approx. 500m SW of Barrenjoey Trig. Station in the suburb of Palm Beach.
A beach adjacent to and coincident with the suburb boundary of Magenta in the Wyong Local Government Area.
ORIGIN: Named after the adjacent suburb of Magenta.
